data.description:
# Intake Brief — Automatically select strong weapons (AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD)

## Problem statement

The target-aware hangar (config) screen already shows the chosen hex boss's
intel and marks every weapon row `▲ EFFECTIVE` (green) / `▼ RESISTED` (red),
but the loadout itself is left entirely to the player: a fresh deployment
carries an **empty** starting-weapon selection, and a returning player may carry
a stale mix that ignores the upcoming boss, so the recorded intel does not
change what the fleet actually flies with. The ask is to make the screen choose
a sensible default — automatically equip the owned weapons that are **strong**
against the target boss, then fill the remaining loadout capacity with a
balanced variety of weapons/power-ups — and to colour the equipped list green
(strong) and red (weak). A fresh (empty) loadout is auto-fitted on open, and an
explicit **apply suggested buildout** button lets the player apply the
recommendation at any time.

## Users

- **Player arriving at a hex** — wants the strongest sensible kit selected for
  them so a hex battle does not begin under-equipped or with a stale loadout.
  - *As a player, when I open the hangar for a hex whose boss the Wave Laser
    counters, I want the Wave Laser already equipped, so I do not have to
    re-derive the intel myself.*
  - *As a player, I want the remaining slots filled with a varied, useful mix
    rather than one family stacked to the cap.*
- **Player who customises** — wants their deliberate choice to survive; the
  automatic fit applies to an empty (default) loadout only, and an explicit
  button applies the suggestion when *they* choose to.
- **Producer/designer** — wants one shared, pure selection rule consumed by the
  game and `GymHangar`, so no scene owns a second loadout policy and the
  gym↔game parity rule holds.
- **Maintainer** — wants the selection to reuse the shipped six-slot cap and
  the shipped matchup resolver (`resolveBossMatchup`) rather than introduce a
  second power/strength model.

## Existing state (verified in code)

- **Matchup display already exists.** `resolveBossMatchup(weaponId, definition)`
  (`src/core/hangarWar/weaponMatchup.ts`) returns `'strong' | 'weak' |
  'neutral'`; `buildHangarWeaponOptions` marks each weapon row with
  `withMatchupMarker` and `rowColour` applies `HANGAR_STRONG_COLOR` /
  `HANGAR_WEAK_COLOR` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`). The colouring
  part of the seed intent is **already satisfied for weapon rows**; only
  weapons carry a boss matchup, so power-up rows stay neutral.
- **The default loadout is deliberately empty.** GDD § *Hangar economy and
  unlock tree* and AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D: `activeLoadout.startingWeapons: []`,
  and "owning the free starter weapon never auto-equips it — equipping a
  starter is always a deliberate choice". This item revises that default for the
  pre-battle case: an empty loadout is auto-fitted.
- **A purchase auto-equips.** `purchaseHangarEntry` buys with
  `equipOnPurchase: true`, so bought parts already land owned-and-armed. This
  is a different mechanism from the requested automatic selection.
- **Six shared loadout slots.** `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`
  (`src/core/constants.ts`); weapons and power-ups share the cap.
  `applyHangarWarDeployment` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`) trims
  the combined list (selected weapons first, then owned power-up levels)
  through `capDropIdsToSlotPool` before granting, so an over-full loadout is
  already trimmed silently — the screen can show more selected weapons than the
  run actually carries (AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX).
- **Power-ups are not loadout-selectable today.** Every owned level-bearing
  power-up is granted on deployment (`levels.powerUps`); `HangarLoadout` has
  only `startingWeapons` and `modifiers`. Making power-ups installable is a
  **separate work item** (AH-0MWOV8SMI006W52Z, spawned by producer Q2 = A);
  this item budgets around the auto-granted power-ups.
- **Every deployment has a target hex.** The hangar screen accepts an optional
  `targetHexId` (set when the map opens it via `HexMapScene.openConfig`); with
  none, `selectDeploymentHex` still resolves the weakest unheld hex, so the
  screen almost always has a boss to fit against.
- **No auto-selection exists today.** There is no auto-fit function, no
  "the player customised this loadout" flag, and no variety rule for a > cap
  owned set.
- **Weapon behaviour families.** Weapons expose behaviour descriptors
  (`aoe`, `bounce`, `hitscan`, `splits`, `orbit`, plain projectiles) in
  `src/utils/weapons.ts`; the variety rule can key on these rather than invent
  a taxonomy.

## Desired change

1. Add a **pure auto-loadout selector** that, given the payload, the target hex
   definition and the catalogue, returns a starting-weapon selection under this
   rule (producer Q3 = "A then C"):
   - include every owned weapon whose matchup is `strong` against the boss;
   - never include a `weak` weapon by auto-selection;
   - enforce the **variety cap**: at most one weapon per behaviour family
     (spread / beam / bounce / split / orbit / AoE);
   - then prefer, in order: `strong`, at least one defensive power-up that the
     deployment will auto-grant, and the highest permanent level;
   - fill toward the shared six-slot cap, budgeting for the owned power-ups that
     will also consume slots at grant time, and never exceed the cap.
2. Apply the selector **automatically only when the loadout is at its default
   (empty) state** (producer Q1 = B), so a deliberate loadout is preserved.
3. Provide an explicit **apply suggested buildout** button that renders the
   suggested selection and applies it when the player activates it (producer Q1
   = B, explicit action). The button is available regardless of whether the
   current loadout is empty.
4. Keep the manual toggles working after auto-selection, and keep the six-slot
   display honest (the selected list should not claim more slots than the run
   will grant).
5. Preserve the equipped-list colours: strong rows green, weak rows red, always
   paired with a non-colour glyph tag (CVD policy); the gym renders the same
   model read-only (gym↔game parity).
6. Update the design-of-record wording (GDD § Hangar economy and unlock tree,
   `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, module JSDoc) to state the auto-fit-when-empty rule,
   the apply-suggested-buildout button and the variety rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Strong weapons are auto-equipped when the loadout is empty.**
      Opening the hangar screen ahead of a battle with an empty loadout on a hex
      whose authored `weaknesses` name an owned weapon selects that weapon in
      `activeLoadout.startingWeapons` (via `resolveBossMatchup === 'strong'`);
      pinned by a pure selector test.
- [ ] **AC2 — Weak weapons are never auto-selected.** An owned weapon whose
      matchup is `weak` is never added by the auto-selector, and is not forced
      into the selection by the fill step.
- [ ] **AC3 — Variety then preference (Q3 = A then C).** The selector applies at
      most one weapon per behaviour family, then prefers `strong`, then at least
      one defensive power-up the deployment will auto-grant, then the highest
      permanent level, and fills toward the shared six-slot cap
      (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`) without exceeding it — accounting for the owned
      power-ups that also consume slots at grant time.
- [ ] **AC4 — A deliberate loadout is preserved; the button applies it on
      demand.** Auto-fit runs only when the loadout is at its default (empty)
      state, so a hand-picked loadout is never silently overwritten; an explicit
      **apply suggested buildout** button renders the suggestion and applies it
      when activated, for any loadout.
- [ ] **AC5 — Manual control is preserved.** After auto-selection the player can
      still toggle any owned weapon.
- [ ] **AC6 — Equipped list colour semantics.** The equipped/loadout list
      colours strong rows green and weak rows red, always paired with a
      non-colour glyph tag (never colour-only, repo CVD policy), and rows with
      no matchup verdict stay neutral. The gym renders the identical model.
- [ ] **AC7 — One shared, pure rule.** The selector is pure and Phaser-free,
      lives in the shared core/model (not scene code), is consumed by the game
      and `GymHangar`, and reuses `resolveBossMatchup`, the shipped catalogue
      and the shared slot-cap helper — no second matchup or slot rule.
- [ ] **AC8 — Determinism and idempotence.** The selector is deterministic for
      a given (payload, target, catalogue) — no wall-clock, no unseeded draws —
      and re-applying it does not duplicate entries or oscillate the selection.
- [ ] **AC9 — Automated tests cover every behaviour above**, and the
      changed-scope test gate passes.
- [ ] **AC10 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
      the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or
      docs site entries (GDD § Hangar economy and unlock tree,
      `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, module JSDoc).
- [ ] **AC11 — Full project test suite.** Full project test suite must pass with
      the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** The selection rule must be consumed by the
  game and every gym that renders the hangar screen; `GymHangar` renders the
  same model read-only. No per-scene copy.
- **Reuse the shipped rules.** Matchup verdicts come from
  `resolveBossMatchup`; slot accounting from `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` /
  `capDropIdsToSlotPool`; ownership from the pure economy. No new power model.
- **CVD policy.** Colour is never the only signal — the `▲ EFFECTIVE` /
  `▼ RESISTED` glyph tag stays primary.
- **No silent divergence from the six-slot cap.** The selected loadout must
  never present more counted kinds than the run will grant.
- **Determinism.** No wall-clock or unseeded randomness.
- **Scope guard.** Do not re-tune weapon balance, change the matchup resolver,
  or redesign the unlock tree here; those are separate items. Making power-ups
  loadout-selectable is AH-0MWOV8SMI006W52Z, not this item. Do not widen into
  the combat effects of strengths/weaknesses (AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/weaponMatchup.ts` — reuse `resolveBossMatchup` (read-only).
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — the model builder, the
  apply-suggested-buildout row/button and the equipped-list rendering.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — owned-entry resolution and loadout
  helpers; the new pure selector likely lives in or beside this module.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — the six-slot grant trim the
  selector must agree with.
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — `capDropIdsToSlotPool` / `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`
  (read-only).
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — behaviour descriptors (`aoe`, `bounce`, `hitscan`,
  `splits`, `orbit`) the variety rule keys on (read-only).
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — applies the selection and persists the payload.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.ts` — read-only parity render.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/*.test.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/*.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` — pure-selector and render tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — § Hangar economy and unlock tree
  (default-empty wording).
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — parity matrix note.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — the "apply suggested buildout" button clutters the screen.** The
  hangar screen already has DEPLOY / HEX MAP / RESTART rows; mitigation: place
  the new control with the loadout section and keep it in the focus order
  consistently.
- **Risk — empty-loadout detection.** "Default/empty" must mean the shipped
  default (`startingWeapons: []`), not "no strong weapon found". Mitigation:
  auto-fit triggers only when `startingWeapons` is empty; the button covers
  every other case.
- **Risk — power-ups are not selectable yet.** The selector can only budget
  around auto-granted power-ups until AH-0MWOV8SMI006W52Z lands. Mitigation:
  the budget rule is written against the grant list so it becomes selectable
  later without a rewrite.
- **Risk — vague "balanced variety".** Resolved by producer Q3 = A then C; the
  rule keys on shipped behaviour descriptors, not a new taxonomy.
- **Risk — colour-only meaning.** Mitigation: the glyph tag is mandatory (CVD).
- **Risk — scope creep.** Rebalancing weapons, changing the matchup rule, or
  making strengths/weaknesses affect combat are separate items — record as
  linked work, not scope.
- **Assumption A1 — "strong" means `resolveBossMatchup === 'strong'`** (the
  existing display rule, player-centric: a weapon in the boss's `weaknesses`).
- **Assumption A2 — "slots" means the shared six-slot loadout cap.**
- **Assumption A3 — the colouring requirement is shipped for weapon rows**;
  this item preserves it and extends it only where the equipped list is
  changed.
- **Assumption A4 — the automatic selection is a pre-battle default, not a
  mid-run rule**, so it belongs in the hangar model, not the combat core.

## Related work

- AH-0MWOV8SMI006W52Z — Hangar: make owned power-ups installable in the
  deployment loadout (open, discovered-from this item) — the producer's Q2 = A
  follow-on.
- AH-0MWMT4NJV001PX8Y — Weapon-vs-boss matchup resolver (completed) — the
  `strong`/`weak` rule this item reuses.
- AH-0MWMT4QXF0095CBN — Target-aware config screen model and render
  (completed) — the intel block and per-row matchup marking.
- AH-0MWMT4STK001PSK4 — Gym parity and documentation (completed) — the
  gym↔game rendering contract.
- AH-0MWMT4S5U001EGDF — Hex map routes into the config screen (completed) —
  the `targetHexId` path that makes the screen "ahead of a battle".
- AH-0MWOQSV7P002IC5Y — Weak/Resist on hangar equip is misleading (open,
  plan_complete) — sibling: it suppresses the highlight on rows the player
  cannot act on; this item changes *what is selected*, not the highlight
  policy. Not a duplicate.
- AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX — Loadout can exceed the six-slot cap (completed) — the
  cap and trim rule the selector must honour.
- AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9 — Hex War doesn't add initial loadout to slots
  (completed) — deployment → HUD grant path.
- AH-0MWB8VDU4007G1LQ — Model the per-ring deployment loadout (completed) —
  precedent for "equip every owned weapon (slot-capped)" as a modelled loadout;
  this item adds boss-aware selection to that idea.
- AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D — the default-empty loadout decision this item revises.
- AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ — Make hex strengths and weaknesses matter in combat
  (open) — the mechanical matchup; out of scope here (display-only per
  AH-0MWMT4NJV001PX8Y assumption A7).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` § Hangar economy and unlock tree.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D § Attract mode (auto-select).

## Impact

A player opening the hangar before a hex battle gets a loadout already fitted
to the boss — strong weapons equipped, weak ones left behind, remaining slots
usefully filled — with an explicit button to re-apply the suggestion, so they
can deploy with confidence without re-deriving the intel by hand.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (RESOLVED) — Trigger and override policy.** When should the automatic
  selection run, and what happens to a hand-picked loadout? Options: A every
  open (persisted); B only when the loadout is default/empty; C behind an
  explicit action; D open but transient.
  - *Answer (producer, 2026-11-20):* **B — auto-fit only when the loadout is at
    its default/empty state — plus provide a button to apply the suggested
    buildout.**
  - *Interpretation:* auto-fit on open when `startingWeapons` is empty, and an
    explicit **apply suggested buildout** button that always renders and applies
    the suggestion on demand. *Source:* interactive reply "1. B (provide a
    button to apply the suggestest buildout)".

- **Q2 (RESOLVED) — Do "power-ups" become loadout-selectable?** Options: A
  budget only; B add power-up selection (large, likely a separate item).
  - *Answer (producer, 2026-11-20):* **A — budget only; create a separate work
    item to add any power-ups that are installable.**
  - *Follow-on:* created **AH-0MWOV8SMI006W52Z — Hangar: make owned power-ups
    installable in the deployment loadout** (feature, discovered-from this
    item). *Source:* interactive reply "2. A - create a separate work item to
    add any power-ups that are installable".

- **Q3 (RESOLVED) — What is "balanced variety"?** Options: A one per behaviour
  family then catalogue order; B round-robin across strong then neutral; C
  prefer strong, then ≥1 defensive power-up, then highest permanent level.
  - *Answer (producer, 2026-11-20):* **A then C.**
  - *Interpretation:* apply the variety cap first (at most one weapon per
    behaviour family), then the preference ordering (strong → at least one
    defensive power-up → highest permanent level) to fill the remaining slots.
    *Source:* interactive reply "3. A then C".

- **Q4 (RESOLVED by repo research) — Does the "colour strong/weak" requirement
  need new work?** The per-row matchup marker (`▲ EFFECTIVE` / `▼ RESISTED`)
  and the strong/weak row colours already ship in `hangarScreen.ts`
  (`withMatchupMarker`, `rowColour`, `HANGAR_STRONG_COLOR` /
  `HANGAR_WEAK_COLOR`). Only weapons carry a boss matchup, so power-up rows are
  neutral. This item preserves that behaviour and covers it with the equipped
  list it changes; no new colour rule is introduced unless the producer asks.
  *Source:* `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/weaponMatchup.ts`, AH-0MWMT4QXF0095CBN /
  AH-0MWMT4STK001PSK4 (completed).

**Research summary:** Inspected `weaponMatchup.ts`, `hangarScreen.ts`
(`buildHangarScreenModel`, `buildHangarWeaponOptions`, `rowColour`),
`hangarDeployment.ts` (`buildHangarDeployment`, `applyHangarWarDeployment`,
six-slot trim), `hangarEconomy.ts` (`resolveActiveLoadout`), `types.ts`
(`HangarLoadout`), `slots.ts` (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`, `capDropIdsToSlotPool`),
`HangarScene.ts`, `HexMapScene.ts` (`openConfig`), `hangarCatalogue.ts`,
`hexRingDefinitions.ts` and `utils/weapons.ts` (owned weapons/power-ups, ring
grants and behaviour descriptors); `docs/Game Design Document.md` § Hangar
economy and unlock tree (default-empty loadout) and
`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D (attract auto-select). Duplicate
check run (`wl search` for auto-equip/strong weapons, loadout slots, target
intel matchup): the closest items are the completed matchup/intel work and the
open AH-0MWOQSV7P002IC5Y (highlight-on-non-actionable rows) — related, not
duplicates.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D** – Hangar War deployments start with no extra weapons in the loadout (default weapon only) (completed)
- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** – Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene (completed)
- **AH-0MWOV8SMI006W52Z** – Hangar: make owned power-ups installable in the deployment loadout (open)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mvvf0pov001jnkx, 0mvzj6v1j001da9d, 0mwcfkhwd002rkx9, 0mwl5376h001wjfz, 0mwmt4s5u001egdf (+516 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mvvf0pov001jnkx, 0mwmt4s5u001egdf, 0mwmt4stk001psk4, ac1, ac2 (+469 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+408 more)

## Plan decomposition (plan skill, 2026-11-20)

Decomposed into seven vertical slices, created in test-first dependency order
(each pair is a red test slice followed by the implementation that turns it
green):

1. AH-0MWOWDBD90045VK0 — Auto-loadout selector contract tests (task, red)
2. AH-0MWOWDNW7001C5X6 — Pure boss-aware auto-loadout selector (feature)
3. AH-0MWOWDWAG007MBY1 — Hangar model and render contract tests (task, red)
4. AH-0MWOWEF3Q008BO5J — Hangar model: auto-fit and suggested buildout row (feature)
5. AH-0MWOWEPO2004B0MR — Hangar screen: auto-fit on open and buildout button (feature)
6. AH-0MWOWEYZQ006IR9T — Document the auto-fit loadout rule (docs)
7. AH-0MWOWF6N5008ZYAJ — Verify auto-loadout parity and full suite (task)

Dependency edges: 2→1, 3→2, 4→3, 5→4, 6→4, 6→5, 7→5, 7→6.

**Resolved during planning (no producer input needed):**

- *Defensive power-up classification* (the effort/risk report's open unknown):
  the shipped `UPGRADE_STAT_BUCKETS` table already classifies the defensive
  kinds (Shield, Force Field, Thorn Field, Bomb, Smart Bomb, Phase Shift) into
  the `armour` bucket. The selector keys defensiveness on that existing row —
  no new taxonomy and no new table.
- *Selector placement*: a new pure module
  `src/core/hangarWar/hangarAutoLoadout.ts` beside the economy, so
  `hangarScreen.ts` keeps its "no selection logic in scene code" rule.
- *Button placement*: with the loadout section, inside the keyboard focus order
  after the loadout options and before `▶ DEPLOY` (the intake risk mitigation).
- *Model purity*: `buildHangarScreenModel` stays pure — it publishes
  `suggestedLoadout` and the buildout row; `HangarScene` performs the
  auto-fit-on-open and the button apply, persisting through the single
  `saveHangarWarPayload` write.

**Open unknowns carried into implementation (non-blocking):**
whether the buildout row should stay in the keyboard focus order or be

# Replace in-repo video processing with the `vidc` CLI

**Issue type:** task · **Priority:** high

## User story

As a maintainer, I want AI_Hell to stop owning its own FFmpeg video-processing
pipeline and instead delegate video compilation to the `vidc` CLI
(`video_compiler`), so that video processing has a single maintained home and
this repository contains only game, capture and telemetry code.

## Background

The repository's post-capture video processing lives in the promo compiler:
`scripts/compile-promo.mjs` (FFmpeg argv planning, per-junction
`xfade`/`acrossfade`, VP9/Opus encoding, probe + brightness + pace validation)
plus its pool inventory (`scripts/list-capture-pool.mjs`) and their tests and
docs. `vidc` (cloned at `../video_compiler`) is the replacement engine: it
discovers clips, orders them, probes with `ffprobe`, and renders one normalised
MP4 with a single FFmpeg invocation, supporting formats and render profiles.

Capture (Playwright `MediaRecorder` → WebM), the capture-time probe/seek/remux
helpers and the action-intensity series export are **capture tooling**, not the
post-capture video-processing pipeline, and stay.

## Decisions

- No backward compatibility: the bespoke compiler, its selection/validation
  logic, its manifests and its tests are deleted rather than kept beside vidc.
- Deliverables become MP4 (vidc's native output), replacing the legacy
  VP9/Opus WebM deliverables.
- Missing vidc capabilities surface during this migration are tracked in the
  `video_compiler` project as **high priority** items and synced:
  - `VC-0MWNOFIBI007J8UK` — render integration honours clip bounds
    (`source_range` in/out trimming).
  - `VC-0MWNW4SPX002J2SE` — transition-aware filter graph (per-junction
    `xfade`/`acrossfade`).
  - `VC-0MWNW4SYJ009XMIP` — compile/render transition hand-off.
  (The automated highlight selection is intentionally dropped with the legacy
  pipeline; vidc owns editing.)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` and its type/test files are removed, along
      with `scripts/list-capture-pool.mjs` and its type/test files.
- [ ] A new thin renderer (`scripts/render-promo.mjs`) forwards to
      `vidc render` (binary overridable via `--vidc` / `VIDC_BIN`), forwards
      subprocess output and exit code, supports `--dir`, `--output`,
      `--pattern`, `--format` (repeatable), `--fade-duration`, `--resolution`,
      `--fps`, `--overwrite`, `--dry-run`, `--json` and `--help`.
- [ ] The renderer is covered by unit tests (mocked subprocess) for argv
      forwarding, exit-code propagation, missing-binary remediation and
      `--json`/`--dry-run` passthrough.
- [ ] `package.json` drops the legacy `list:pool` entry and points
      `capture:promo` at the new renderer.
- [ ] The legacy video-processing documentation is removed: the
      "Pool inventory" and "Compiling a promo package" sections of
      `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, and the highlight-selection / pace-band
      sections (§7.5, §7.6) of `docs/dev/action-intensity.md`, with
      cross-references and `src/promoCompileDocs.test.ts` updated or removed.
- [ ] Doc guards that imported constants from the deleted compiler
      (`src/actionIntensityDocs.test.ts`, `scripts/promo-scenarios.test.ts`,
      `scripts/capture-scenarios.test.ts`) are updated to use the surviving
      editorial-category vocabulary.
- [ ] `npm run build` and the changed-scope test gate pass.

## Impact

Maintainers no longer carry a bespoke FFmpeg promo pipeline in AI_Hell: video
compilation is delegated to the maintained `vidc` CLI.

## Assumptions

- Capture recording, capture-time probing/remuxing and action-intensity series
  export are capture tooling, not the post-capture video-processing pipeline.
- MP4 is acceptable as the deliverable container for promos.
- Automated highlight selection is out of scope after the migration and is
  removed with the legacy compiler; vidc's timeline editing is the forward path
  once its trimming/transition items land.

## Key Files

- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs`, `scripts/compile-promo.d.mts`
- `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts`, `scripts/compile-promo.e2e.test.ts`
- `scripts/list-capture-pool.mjs`, `scripts/list-capture-pool.d.mts`, `scripts/list-capture-pool.test.ts`
- `scripts/render-promo.mjs`, `scripts/render-promo.d.mts`, `scripts/render-promo.test.ts`
- `package.json`
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `docs/dev/action-intensity.md`, `README.md`
- `src/promoCompileDocs.test.ts`, `src/actionIntensityDocs.test.ts`
- `scripts/promo-scenarios.mjs`, `scripts/promo-scenarios.test.ts`
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs`, `scripts/capture-scenarios.test.ts`, `scripts/capture-scenario-schema.mjs`

# Intake Brief — Hangar: make owned power-ups installable in the deployment loadout

## Problem statement

A deployment currently installs **every** owned level-bearing power-up
automatically: `buildHangarDeployment` copies the whole
`hangarPermanentLevels(hangar).powerUps` list into `powerUpLevels`, and
`applyHangarWarDeployment` grants all of it (trimmed only by the shared
six-slot cap). Because `HangarLoadout` holds just `startingWeapons` and
`modifiers`, the hangar screen has no way to express *which* power-ups a
deployment installs — so a fleet that owns more counted kinds than the cap has
its build silently chosen for it by catalogue order.

## Users

- **Player preparing a deployment** — wants to curate the build for the
  upcoming hex.
  - *As a player, when I own five power-ups but want two of them installed
    alongside four weapons, I want to pick those two, so the six slots go to
    the kit I chose rather than to whatever I bought first.*
  - *As a player, I want the loadout I see on the hangar screen to be exactly
    the kit the run launches with, so I am not surprised mid-battle.*
- **Player with an existing save** — wants to keep flying what they flew
  before this feature, without re-fitting anything.
- **Designer / maintainer** — wants one selection model consumed by the game
  and `GymHangar`, reusing the shipped slot cap and permanent-grant seams, with
  no second power-up budget and no schema bump.

## Existing state (verified in code)

- **The model has no power-up slot.** `HangarLoadout`
  (`src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`) is `{ startingWeapons: string[]; modifiers:
  string[] }`; `DeployedShip` mirrors the same three fields (hull +
  `startingWeapons` + `modifiers`).
- **Every owned level-bearing power-up is auto-installed.**
  `buildHangarDeployment` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`) maps
  `levels.powerUps` wholesale into `powerUpLevels`;
  `applyHangarWarDeployment` then caps the combined weapons+power-up list
  through `capDropIdsToSlotPool` and grants each row through
  `grantPermanentPowerUp` / `grantPermanentWeapon` (one grant per level), so
  the leftover rows are dropped by cap order, not by player choice.
- **Persistence is field-presence tolerant.** `parseLoadout`
  (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts`) rebuilds the loadout from known
  fields only and defaults a missing/wrong-shaped loadout to empty; the payload
  is versioned (`version: 1`) but the GDD documents "migration is decided by
  field presence", so a new optional field needs no version bump.
- **Resolution filters to owned entries.** `resolveActiveLoadout` /
  `equipLoadout` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) drop catalogue-unknown
  or unowned ids, so a corrupt save can never install an unowned power-up.
- **The selector is weapons + modifiers only.** `buildHangarScreenModel`
  produces `HangarWeaponOption` and `HangarModifierOption` rows
  (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) with `toggleHangarWeapon` /
  `toggleHangarModifier` handlers; `GymHangar` renders the same model
  read-only, so any new row appears in both.
- **Consumption spends hull, weapons and modifiers only.**
  `consumeDeployedShip` removes the flown hull, starting weapons and modifiers
  (plus their bought level rows) and resets `activeLoadout` to
  `{ startingWeapons: [], modifiers: [] }`; power-up level rows are **not**
  spent today.

## Desired change

- Add an optional power-up selection to `HangarLoadout` and mirror it on
  `DeployedShip`, `parseLoadout` and `equipLoadout` — no schema/version bump.
- Render owned, level-bearing power-ups as toggleable rows in the hangar
  deployment selector, with the same equipped/unequipped affordance as weapons,
  through a `toggleHangarPowerUp` handler that routes through `equipLoadout`.
- Resolve the selection in `buildHangarDeployment` (only the selected rows reach
  `powerUpLevels`) and keep `applyHangarWarDeployment`'s grant loop and
  six-slot trim as the single grant seam.
- Make the displayed loadout equal the granted loadout: apply the same
  `capDropIdsToSlotPool` trimming in the screen model and render
  non-admitted rows as blocked/non-actionable rather than silently differing.
- Expose the selection to the auto-loadout selector (parent
  AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD) so its "balanced variety" fill can include power-ups.
- Keep gym↔game parity: `GymHangar` renders the same model read-only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Owned level-bearing power-ups appear as toggleable rows in the hangar deployment selector, with a clear equipped/unequipped state.
- [ ] A deployment grants exactly the selected power-ups (and their permanent levels); deselected power-ups are not granted.
- [ ] The combined selected weapons + power-ups respect the shared six-slot cap, and the displayed loadout matches what the run grants.
- [ ] A save written before this feature (no selection field) deploys with the existing behaviour, with no schema bump.
- [ ] The auto-loadout selector can select power-ups once this lands.
- [ ] The game and `GymHangar` render from the same model.
- [ ] Automated tests cover the model, the resolve/grant path and the gym parity (including a red-first test for the new selection field and its default).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the GDD (§8.1 payload, six-slot loadout), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Reuse the shipped slot cap (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` via `capDropIdsToSlotPool`)
  and the shipped permanent-grant seams; no second power-up budget.
- Additive persisted field only, in the `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels`
  pattern; empty/absent must stay legal and must not throw.
- Do not change power-up balance, the six-slot semantics, or which kinds carry
  a permanent level (consumables and field-pickup-only kinds stay unselectable).
- Installation is a loadout choice, not a new spend: the existing
  `consumeDeployedShip` rule is unchanged — a flown hull, starting weapons and
  modifiers are spent, and installed power-ups are not.
- No Phaser or storage access in the pure core/deployment modules; `GymHangar`
  stays read-only (no purchase/toggle handlers).

## Assumptions and decisions

- **A1 — Tri-state field.** The new field is optional: `undefined` (a save
  written before this feature) means "not chosen yet" and keeps today's
  behaviour (every owned level-bearing power-up installs); `[]` means a
  deliberate empty selection and installs none; a populated list installs
  exactly those ids. This keeps AC4 satisfiable while letting a player empty
  the selection — the same shape `HangarLoadout.startingWeapons` already has.
- **A2 — Selection is persisted in `activeLoadout`,** not as a parallel
  top-level field, so `resolveActiveLoadout` / `equipLoadout` remain the single
  ownership filter and a corrupt save cannot install an unowned power-up.
- **A3 — Display equals grant via the shared cap predicate,** applied in the
  model as well as at grant time; grant-time trimming stays as the backstop for
  launch data from another build.
- **A4 — Installed power-ups are not consumed** (see Constraints). Power-up
  levels are permanent purchases; spending them per sortie would be an economy
  change this item explicitly excludes.
- **A5 — No producer questions were needed:** the seed description, the parent
  item (AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD) and the code above resolve every open point; the
  four decisions above are documented for confirmation at review.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Display/grant drift** (the reason AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX existed): mitigated by
  A3 — one predicate (`capDropIdsToSlotPool`) drives both the model and the
  grant, with a test asserting the two sets are equal.
- **Retro-fitting existing saves:** a naive default of "select nothing" would
  strip power-ups from every existing player's next sortie. Mitigated by A1
  (`undefined` ⇒ today's behaviour) and a test on a pre-feature payload.
- **Consumption regression:** adding a field to `DeployedShip` /
  `HangarLoadout` touches `consumeDeployedShip`'s reset shape. Mitigated by
  keeping the consumption rule unchanged (A4) and asserting the reset keeps the
  new field well-formed.
- **Row-count/layout pressure:** the right column already lays out weapons and
  modifiers by index (`hangarRightColumnLayout`); extra rows change nothing
  semantically but must not overlap. Mitigated by layout tests at a full
  catalogue.
- **Scope creep:** boss-matchup colouring for power-ups, auto-fit heuristics,
  and per-battle power-up spending belong to other items (parent
  AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD / AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY). They are recorded there, not
  pulled into this one.

## Key Files (predicted)

**Key Files:**
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — `HangarLoadout` and `DeployedShip` gain the optional power-up selection.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — `resolveActiveLoadout` / `equipLoadout` filter the selection to owned, level-bearing ids; `consumeDeployedShip` reset shape stays valid.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — `parseLoadout` reads the field with presence-based defaulting (A1), no version bump.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — `buildHangarDeployment` resolves only the selected rows into `powerUpLevels`; `applyHangarWarDeployment` cap/grant seam unchanged.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — `HangarPowerUpOption` rows, cap-aware `buildHangarScreenModel`, `toggleHangarPowerUp`, keyboard/focus wiring and layout.
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — the shared `capDropIdsToSlotPool` / level-bearing-kind predicates the model and the grant both use (no new budget).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.ts` — parity: renders the same read-only model.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.test.ts`, `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.test.ts` (or nearest equivalents), `src/test/sixSlotLoadoutFixtures.ts` — red-first coverage of the model, the resolve/grant path and the parity.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §8.1 payload field and the six-slot loadout section.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — the `GymHangar` row (guarded by `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts`).
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — Candidate D loadout description, if it enumerates loadout fields.

## Related work

- **AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD** — Automatically select strong weapons (parent; this
  item was spawned from producer decision Q2 = A to make power-ups
  installable, because the auto-fill can only choose from an installable set).
- **AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX** — Loadout can exceed the six-slot cap (completed;
  established the shared cap predicate used here).
- **AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9** — Hex War doesn't add initial loadout to slots
  (completed; established the `applyHangarWarDeployment` registry grant seam).
- **AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D** — default-empty loadout decision (an empty selection
  is a legal deployment — the precedent for A1's `[]` case).
- **AH-0MWI5AG1X0007XZH** — Persist permanent levels through store and grant
  seam (completed; the `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` pattern this field
  follows).
- **AH-0MWB8VDU4007G1LQ** — Model the per-ring deployment loadout (completed).
- **AH-0MWKXPO5A007R5RB** — Power-up unlock-tree kind, owned set and authored
  entry (completed; the owned-set source the selector reads).
- **AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY** — Post-MVP Hangar War: hull upgrade bays as a reward
  axis (open; adjacent loadout work, not blocking).

## Impact

Players can curate which owned power-ups a deployment installs, so the loadout
they see is the loadout they fly.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Q1 — Does the new selection default to "all owned" or "none" for existing
saves?**
Answer (derived from the seed brief, no producer round needed): **all owned**,
via an optional (`undefined`) field. Evidence: the seed description's "preserve
the current default behaviour for saves without the new field"; current
behaviour verified in `buildHangarDeployment` (`powerUpLevels:
levels.powerUps.map(...)`) and `applyHangarWarDeployment`. Research: a "none"
default would silently strip power-ups from every live save on the next
sortie, contradicting the explicit constraint. Related:
AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D (an *explicit* empty selection is still legal). Decision
recorded as assumption A1.

**Q2 — Does installing a power-up mean the fleet spends it on battle end, like
a weapon?**
Answer: **No.** `consumeDeployedShip` spends the hull, starting weapons and
modifiers (and their bought level rows) and never power-up level rows; power-ups
are permanent level purchases and the item's constraints forbid changing
power-up balance or economy. Decision recorded as assumption A4; the
consumption rule is left byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Q3 — Where does the selection live: a new top-level hangar field or inside
`HangarLoadout`?**
Answer: **inside `HangarLoadout`** (plus `DeployedShip`). Rationale:
`resolveActiveLoadout` / `equipLoadout` are the shipped ownership filters, so a
parallel field would need a second filter and could install an unowned
power-up. Decision recorded as assumption A2.

**Q4 — Does the six-slot cap get enforced at selection time, at grant time, or
both?**
Answer: **both, from one predicate.** `applyHangarWarDeployment` already trims
weapons+power-ups through `capDropIdsToSlotPool`
(AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX); the screen model must apply the same predicate so the
displayed loadout equals the granted loadout (AC3), with grant-time trimming
kept as the backstop for launch data from another build. Decision recorded as
assumption A3.

**Q5 — Which power-up kinds are selectable?**
Answer: only **level-bearing** kinds — the same set `powerUpLevels` already
carries. Consumables (charge pools) and field-pickup-only kinds carry no
permanent level and are excluded, per the existing doc comment on
`HangarWarDeployment.powerUpLevels` (AH-0MWI5AG1X0007XZH AC5). No new rule.

**Plan revision note (2026-11-20):** re-read during planning; Q1–Q5 and
assumptions A1–A5 are unchanged and were reused without a new producer
round. No question was re-asked and no entry was duplicated.

**Open questions for the producer:** none. Items Q1–Q5 are answered from the
seed brief, the parent item and the shipped code, and are recorded as
assumptions A1–A5 for confirmation at review.

## Plan

Decomposed into eight child features in dependency order — one red-first
contract suite, five implementation slices (model → deployment → screen model →
scene wiring, plus the auto-loadout seam), the gym-parity slice and a docs/suite
closure. Each child is a vertical slice carrying its own tests and docs touch.

| # | Child | Type | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Red-first tests: power-up loadout selection (AH-0MWOWO5WX005HKWY) | task | — |
| 2 | Power-up loadout field and persistence (AH-0MWOWO6IJ006X5CC) | feature | 1 |
| 3 | Deployment grants only selected power-ups (AH-0MWOWO753006K7NJ) | feature | 2 |
| 4 | Hangar model: power-up selector rows (AH-0MWOWO7VY005BOZA) | feature | 3 |
| 5 | Hangar scene: power-up wiring and layout (AH-0MWOWO8KG006K0WJ) | feature | 4 |
| 6 | GymHangar parity for power-up rows (AH-0MWOWO9AS003FWJI) | feature | 4 |
| 7 | Auto-loadout power-up selection seam (AH-0MWOWO9X2005PB1G) | feature | 2, 3 |
| 8 | Power-up loadout docs and suite gate (AH-0MWOWOAJL005RN6M) | docs | 5, 6 |

**Vertical-slice phasing:** children 2–6 each cut through the layers they touch
(pure model + store + tests; deployment + tests; screen model + tests; scene +
layout/focus tests; gym + parity docs + guard). Between phases the next child's
description is reviewed and updated before implementation. Docs that describe
final behaviour (GDD, candidate doc, module JSDoc) land last in child 8 rather
than being scattered.

**Reuse, not reinvention:** the shared cap predicate (`capDropIdsToSlotPool`,
AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX), the permanent-grant seam (`applyHangarWarDeployment`,
AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9), the ownership filter (`ownedEntriesOf` /
`resolveActiveLoadout`) and the payload's presence-based migration are consumed
unchanged — no second power-up budget, no schema bump.

**Sequencing note for child 5:** the right column currently holds hulls,
weapons, modifiers and the compact saved-build block, and no viewport guard
exists yet; child 5 owns the full-catalogue layout test and may reduce the row
step (an allowed fix inside that child) if the new section overflows.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-20T11:40Z — plan run (downtime dispatch): read the intake brief and
  verified the shipped seams in `types.ts`, `hangarWarStore.ts`,
  `hangarEconomy.ts`, `hangarDeployment.ts`, `hangarScreen.ts`, `slots.ts` and
  `GymHangar.ts`; created 8 child features in test-first dependency order;
  wired 9 blocking edges; ran the six automated review stages and the AC
  coverage review (100% of the parent's criteria covered by children, no
  auto-created children needed). No new producer questions: the intake's
  Appendix Q1–Q5 answers were reused rather than re-asked.

# Intensity-arc promo timeline: generate the `.otio` from action-intensity series

**Issue type:** feature · **Priority:** high
**discovered-from:AH-0MWOVILCN008HPP2** (the `vidc`-backed `render-promo` thin renderer this extends)

## User story

As a producer I want `npm run capture:promo` to generate a `.otio` sequence that
`vidc` compiles, cut from the recorded action-intensity series — **10 s of high
intensity, 7 s of medium, 7 s of medium+, 10 s of very high** — so the promo is
assembled from measured action instead of filename order, and the edit decision
stays hand-editable and reproducible.

## Target outcome

```bash
npm run capture:promo
```

reads `<run-id>.action.jsonl` and `<run-id>.capture.json` for every captured
clip, selects non-overlapping footage windows matching the four intensity bands,
writes `capture-output/promo.otio` (one `Clip.1` per window, with a
`source_range` in point and a document-relative `media_reference.target_url`),
then hands that document to `vidc render` as its timeline source. `vidc`
compiles it to `capture-output/promo.mp4` with a rendered arc of 34 s.

**The intensity arc is the only behaviour, with no opt-in flag and no
alternative mode.** An intensity-arc flag would be pointless: cut-to-the-action
is what this entry point is *for*, so it is the default and the only path.
There is no "compile every clip in filename order" mode to fall back to.

## Requirements & context

### Why this is not "just concatenate" today

`npm run capture:promo` currently forwards to `vidc render --dir capture-output`,
which compiles every discovered clip, in natural filename order, with a 300 ms
`xfade`/`acrossfade` between each. Nothing reads the intensity series. The
former in-repo highlight selector was deleted in **AH-0MWOUY9IK004QWCU** when
video compilation moved to `vidc`, and `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.5
records the series + join anchor as retained artefacts specifically so a
`vidc`-based editor can consume them. This item resumes that path — in the
tooling layer, not by reintroducing an FFmpeg pipeline.

### Inputs already recorded (no gameplay work)

- `capture-output/<run-id>.action.jsonl` — 10 Hz series, header
  (`schemaVersion`, `runSeed`, `sampleRateHz`, `categories`) plus samples
  `{ t, tick, rawScore, intensity, smoothed, burstiness, breakdown }`.
  Produced by `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` via `scripts/capture-series.mjs`.
- `capture-output/<run-id>.capture.json` — the §7.5 join anchor
  (`capture_started`, `runStartedAt`, `offsetMs`, `approximate`), giving
  `videoTimeMs(t) ≈ t − offsetMs`.

Reuse the existing helpers in `scripts/capture-series.mjs`
(`ACTION_INTENSITY_SERIES_EXTENSION`, `CAPTURE_ANCHOR_EXTENSION`,
`hasActionIntensitySample`, `actionIntensitySeriesFileName`,
`captureAnchorFileName`) — do not re-derive the filenames or re-parse the format.

### Hard external dependency: `vidc` must honour clip bounds

`vidc` compiles a document to a clip **path** only: `compileClips()` in
`src/otio/compile.ts` ignores `source_range`, so a document's in point and
duration are validated by the reader but **not rendered**. Until
**VC-0MWNOFIBI007J8UK** (*Render integration honours clip bounds*, currently
`blocked` in the `video_compiler` worklog) lands, a compiled `.otio` renders
each source file whole and the arc cannot be delivered.

Consequence for this item: the planning/materialisation ACs (series ingest,
band selection, `.otio` emission, determinism) are implementable and unit
testable **now**; the end-to-end rendered-duration AC is gated on
VC-0MWNOFIBI007J8UK. Do **not** work around it by trimming clips with FFmpeg in
this repo — that would reverse AH-0MWOUY9IK004QWCU.

Note also: document-level transitions are not rendered yet either
(`VC-0MWNW4SPX002J2SE`, `VC-0MWNW4T81005YFBJ`), so window joins are **hard
cuts** and the only cross-fade available is `vidc render --fade-duration`.

### Band definitions (defaults, calibrated — not guesses)

`intensity` is bounded in `[0, 1)` by `R/(R+30)`, so bands are fixed thresholds
on it. Measured over the 35 recorded series currently in `capture-output`
(19 991 samples): p50 = 0.45, p75 = 0.55, p90 = 0.62, max = 0.90. Contiguous
availability at candidate thresholds: **≥ 0.70 → 46.2 s** (one clip),
**≥ 0.75 → 25.4 s**, **≥ 0.80 → 4 s pooled**. A "very high ≥ 0.80" band would
therefore be unsatisfiable for 10 s, so the defaults are:

| Band | Default threshold | Target |
|---|---|---|
| medium | `0.40 ≤ I < 0.55` | 7 s |
| medium+ | `0.55 ≤ I < 0.65` | 7 s |
| high | `0.65 ≤ I < 0.75` | 10 s |
| very high | `I ≥ 0.75` | 10 s |

Thresholds and targets live in **one config object** with documented defaults
(the pattern `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §6.6 already establishes for the
metric's own knobs), overridable from the CLI, so the calibration task can
retune them without a code change.

### Selection semantics

- The arc is **high → medium → medium+ → very high** as specified, and the
  bands draw from **non-overlapping** footage (no segment is reused, and no two
  windows overlap inside one source clip).
- Prefer the **fewest windows** per band (one contiguous window where the
  footage allows), minimum window length 1.0 s; windows may come from different
  captures.
- Durability: a band that cannot be filled from the available footage is a
  **hard failure** naming the shortfall (`band, required s, longest available
  s`), never a silently shorter arc.
- Deterministic: identical inputs produce a byte-identical `.otio`; ties are
  broken by clip natural order, then earliest `t`.
- Target durations are measured on the **rendered** timeline: because the join
  is a `--fade-duration` cross fade, the planner compensates (adds
  `(n−1) × fade / n` per band) so the delivered MP4 totals 34 s rather than
  34 s minus the overlaps.

### Emitted document

- Valid OpenTimelineIO 0.16.0 (`Timeline.1` / `Track.1` / `Clip.1`), one video
  track, clips in arc order.
- `media_reference.target_url` relative to the document's directory (so
  `capture-output/promo.otio` names `gameplay-….webm`).
- `source_range.start_time` = in point (rate = series-joined video time),
  `source_range.duration` = window length.
- `metadata` records the planner inputs (band thresholds, fade, per-band
  achieved totals) so an edit is auditable.

### Wiring

- `scripts/render-promo.mjs` **always** plans and writes the timeline; there is
  no flag to select it and nothing else it can do. The existing option surface
  keeps its meanings where they still apply: `--dir` names the directory of
  captures to plan from, `--output` names both the MP4 and (by stem) the
  `.otio`, and `--overwrite`/`--dry-run`/`--json`/`--format`/`--resolution`/
  `--fps`/`--fade-duration`/`--vidc` keep forwarding to `vidc render`.
- `--pattern` narrows **which captures feed the arc** (it is an input filter for
  series discovery, keeping today's default that excludes `.seekable.webm` and
  `.partial.webm`), not a `vidc` discovery pattern, because `vidc` receives a
  document and never discovers clips in this path.
- The generated document is passed to `vidc` as its **timeline source**, not
  `--dir`, so `vidc`'s auto-detected `<output>.otio` path is deliberate rather
  than accidental: the script always rewrites the document (never leaves a
  stale one to drive a render).
- `--dry-run` prints the arc plan and the `vidc` argv, writing nothing.

### Behaviour change (intended, no compatibility shim)

Removing the concat-everything default is deliberate, and its consequences must
be stated in the docs and the CLI help rather than softened by a flag:

- **Only captures with a usable series can appear.** Today 35 of the 56 clips
  in `capture-output` have a series, so ~21 clips silently drop out of the promo.
  The planner warns per skipped clip and fails with an actionable error when no
  usable capture remains.
- **Clip order stops being filename order** — it is arc order by construction.
- **The promo is now shorter than the summed footage**: 34 s delivered by
  design, not "every clip, however many hours that is".
- A plain whole-clip concat remains available by invoking `vidc render --dir`
  directly; that escape hatch belongs to `vidc`, not to this script.

## Key files

- `scripts/render-promo.mjs` — CLI surface, mode switch, `vidc` handoff
- `scripts/render-promo.test.ts` — argv/handoff tests (extend)
- `scripts/intensity-arc.mjs` (new) — pure planner: series ingest, band
  selection, window assembly, duration compensation
- `scripts/intensity-arc.d.mts` (new) — types
- `scripts/intensity-arc.test.ts` (new) — planner tests, synthetic fixtures
- `scripts/otio-write.mjs` (new, or reuse a shared writer) — `.otio` emission
- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.5 and `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` —
  record the new consumer of the series

## Deliverables

- Pure, test-first intensity-arc planner with a documented config object.
- `.otio` emission for the planned sequence, validated against the OTIO 0.16.0
  shape `vidc` reads.
- `capture:promo` wired through to `vidc render` as a document source, with the
  intensity arc as its only behaviour (no flag, no alternative mode).
- Unit tests + docs.

## Constraints

- No FFmpeg/VP9/Opus logic and no video processing in this repo (AH-0MWOUY9IK004QWCU).
- Tooling only (`scripts/`): no gameplay change, no gym↔game parity impact, no
  change to the recorded series format.
- No new dependency for OTIO writing unless a maintained one already exists;
  the document is plain JSON in the pinned schema.

## Dependencies

- `AH-0MWOVILCN008HPP2` — the `vidc`-backed `render-promo` renderer this
  extends (discovered-from; the file exists, item still open).
- **`VC-0MWNOFIBI007J8UK`** (*Render integration honours clip bounds*,
  `video_compiler`, **blocked**) — required for the end-to-end rendered arc.
- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.2–§7.5 artefacts (available today).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (ingest):** the planner loads `<stem>.action.jsonl` +
  `<stem>.capture.json` per capture (honouring `--pattern` as a capture filter),
  skips header-only/sample-less series and clips with a missing or
  `approximate` anchor with exactly one warning each, and fails with an
  actionable error when no usable capture remains. Covered by unit tests over
  committed synthetic fixtures (no browser, no network).
- **AC2 (bands):** the four bands and their 7/7/10/10 s targets live in one
  documented, overridable config object; a band that cannot be filled fails
  naming band, required seconds and the longest available window. Unit tested
  for both the satisfiable and the shortfall case.
- **AC3 (selection):** the chosen windows (a) are non-overlapping within each
  source clip, (b) are ordered high → medium → medium+ → very high, (c) use the
  fewest windows reaching each target with a 1.0 s minimum, and (d) produce a
  rendered-timeline total of 34 s (fade overlap compensated). Asserted on
  synthetic series with known-intensity plateaus plus a property test that no
  window is reused.
- **AC4 (determinism):** running the planner twice on the same inputs produces
  a byte-identical `.otio`; ties resolve by clip natural order then earliest
  `t`. Unit tested by double-run comparison.
- **AC5 (document):** the emitted `.otio` parses as `Timeline.1`/`Track.1`/
  `Clip.1` with one video track, one `Clip.1` per window carrying a
  document-relative `target_url` and a `source_range` whose start/duration equal
  the planned window, and is accepted by `vidc timeline`/`vidc render` with no
  schema diagnostics (checked with `vidc` present, documented as a manual
  verification step).
- **AC6 (wiring):** a bare `npm run capture:promo` generates the document and
  invokes `vidc render` **with that document as its source**; there is no flag
  that selects or disables the arc, and no code path forwards `--dir` to `vidc`
  discovery; `--dry-run` prints the arc plan and `vidc` argv and writes nothing.
  Unit tests assert that the default invocation always passes a document source,
  and the existing argv-forwarding/exit-code/missing-binary tests are rewritten
  to the new contract (not left asserting the removed behaviour).
- **AC7 (end-to-end, gated on VC-0MWNOFIBI007J8UK):** with clip bounds honoured
  by `vidc`, the rendered `promo.mp4` measures 34 s ± 0.5 s and `ffprobe`-per-
  band segment durations land within ± 100 ms of their targets. Blocked until
  that `vc` item lands; recorded as the acceptance run.
- **AC8 (hygiene and docs):** tests written first; full `npm run test` gate
  green; `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.5 and `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`
  document the new consumer, the arc as the sole behaviour and the drop-out of
  captures without a series (including the `vidc render --dir` escape hatch);
  `--help` describes the arc rather than a flag; missing-`vidc` remediation
  (exit 127) behaviour unchanged.

## Assumptions (documented, revisit at implementation)

1. Band thresholds above are calibrated to the current 35-series corpus; only
   ~4 s of footage exists at `I ≥ 0.80`, which is why "very high" is `≥ 0.75`.
2. Selection uses instantaneous `intensity`; window edges are nudged to local
   `smoothed` minima to avoid cutting mid-spike.
3. Arc durations are targets for the **rendered** output, so the planner adds
   fade compensation rather than delivering 34 s minus overlaps.
4. Windows are joined with hard cuts (no document transitions yet); the only
   softening is `--fade-duration`.
5. The arc is a single fixed sequence (no repeat/loop) delivering 34 s total.
6. One `.otio` (`capture-output/promo.otio`) pairs with one MP4, consistent with
   `vidc`'s `<output>.otio` convention.
7. No opt-out by design: the thresholds and targets are tuned by editing the one
   config object (a code change, no rebuild — these are plain Node scripts), not
   by a CLI flag or an environment variable. Calibration therefore never needs
   an alternate code path.
8. `--pattern` keeps its value as a capture-input filter; if review concludes it
   too is pointless now, drop it in the same change rather than leaving a dead
   option.

## Impact

A producer can generate a promo whose cut follows the action it actually
recorded — climbing from a 7-second lull into ten seconds of peak chaos — and
tweak the edit in any OTIO editor instead of hand-picking timestamps.
data.title: Intensity-arc promo timeline: generate the .otio sequence from action-intensity series

## Failure Signature

- Test name: src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts > Demo mode integration (AH-0MUX496TY005FF3P) > AC1/AC3 — the committed steering is held at a human cadence, not every tick
- Failing commit: 93949f6665c1aeed9e082940720012ef74ac771b
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
AssertionError: expected 2 to be 1 // Object.is equality

 ❯ src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts:255:23
    255|     expect(seen.size).toBe(1);

```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout 93949f6665c1aeed9e082940720012ef74ac771b`
2. Run the failing test: `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings -k 'src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts > Demo mode integration (AH-0MUX496TY005FF3P) > AC1/AC3 — the committed steering is held at a human cadence, not every tick'` (or equivalent command)
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item

## Root Cause

The failing assertion (`src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts:255`) samples
`governor.currentIntent()` once per tick over a 10-tick (~167 ms) window and
requires exactly one distinct value. Its `steering()` helper strips only the
`thrust` field before comparing.

`BotInputGovernor.update()` treats the **reverse** request as a fast braking
reflex, exactly like forward thrust: when no new decision is due it copies the
fresh `decision.thrust` / `decision.reverse` onto the held intent every tick
(the `else if (typeof decision.thrust === 'boolean')` branch in
`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`) and then re-runs the human-like press hold. The
committed *bearing* (`dirX`/`dirY` plus the cardinal booleans) is correctly
held for `reactionTimeMs`, but `committed.reverse` can flip once inside the
window.

The test predates the reverse reflex (added by AH-0MV1J0OHP0072XA5 /
AH-0MV2JT0TF008T3OW), so its `steering()` helper carries the stale assumption
that `thrust` is the only per-tick field. The demo run seed is fresh on every
run (`MenuScene.startDemo()` → `PlayScene._initRunSeed()` → `randomSeed()`),
so whether the brain requests reverse inside those ten ticks varies run to
run — hence the intermittent `expected 2 to be 1`.

The failure is a **latent flaky test**, not a regression from 93949f6: that
commit only touched `src/ai/botSteeringLateGameDeterminism.test.ts` and
`docs/PERFORMANCE.md`, neither of which changes demo steering behaviour.

## Implementation Plan

1. In `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`, update the
   `AC1/AC3 — the committed steering is held at a human cadence, not every
   tick` test's `steering()` helper to exclude **both** fast-reflex fields
   (`thrust` and `reverse`) before comparing, leaving the held
   bearing/cardinals (and `longTravel` / `aim`) — the decision the human
   cadence actually governs.
2. Update the inline comment to say that thrust **and** reverse are per-tick
   reflexes; the human cadence applies to the chosen target bearing, and the
   reverse *key press* is humanised by `reversePressMinMs` /
   `reversePressMaxMs`.
3. Optionally pin the demo run seed in this test
   (`scene.start('PlayScene', { demo: true, seed: 42 })`) so its decision
   sequence is reproducible. The assertion is already seed-independent once
   step 1 lands, so this is robustness, not a requirement.
4. Document the reflex-vs-cadence split in `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §9.7
   (reverse thrust): the reverse *request* is re-evaluated every tick just
   like forward thrust; the human-like element is the press-duration hold,
   and the committed target bearing is held for `reactionTimeMs`.
5. Verification: run the changed-scope suite through `/skill:test`
   (`demoMode.integration.test.ts`, `botHumanLike.test.ts`,
   `botSteeringLateGameDeterminism.test.ts`), then let the dev-push gate run
   the full suite.

## Impact

The demo/attract integration suite stops flaking on a behaviour it never meant
to forbid, so a green run again means the demo bot's human cadence is intact
rather than a lucky random seed.

_Original triage note: failing test detected by an agent during an automated
run; may block PR creation for the agent's current work item._

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts > Demo mode integration (AH-0MUX496TY005FF3P) > AC1/AC3 — the committed steering is held at a human cadence, not every tick` passes when run against the latest `dev`.
2. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
4. The test still verifies its original intent — the committed target bearing is held across the reaction window — rather than passing because the comparison was weakened to nothing.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)

## Impact

The demo-mode cadence check now measures only the held steering decision: an in-flight brake no longer reads as a cadence failure, so the suite stops failing intermittently on demo-mode runs.

# Arc planner test corpus and fixture builders

**Issue type:** task · **Priority:** high
**Parent:** AH-0MWPCLYYG007NUJY · test-first scaffolding for the intensity-arc planner.

## Goal

Commit the synthetic fixture corpus and pure builder helpers that every
intensity-arc test relies on, so the planner, the `.otio` writer and the CLI
wiring are unit-tested with **no browser, no network and no capture footage**.

## Scope

- Committed fixtures under `scripts/fixtures/intensity-arc/`:
  - `plateaus` — one capture whose samples form known-intensity plateaus
    covering all four bands (medium 0.40–0.55, medium+ 0.55–0.65, high
    0.65–0.75, very high ≥ 0.75) with enough contiguous duration per band
    (≥ the 7/7/10/10 s targets).
  - `short-band` — a series where "very high ≥ 0.75" totals < 10 s (the
    shortfall case).
  - `header-only` — a header line and nothing else.
  - `header-only`/`no-samples` — a series whose sample lines carry no usable
    `intensity`.
  - `approx` — an `approximate: true` join anchor.
  - `two-runs` — two capture stems whose bands must be pooled (windows drawn
    from different captures in one plan).
- A pure builder module (`scripts/intensity-arc-fixtures.mjs`) that turns a
  plateau spec `[{ fromT, toT, intensity }]` into a valid series, reusing
  `serialiseActionIntensitySeries` / `actionIntensitySeriesLine` from
  `scripts/capture-series.mjs` so the fixture format can never drift from the
  recorded one. No new format is invented.
- A short documented fixture contract (module comment) so later items add
  cases rather than ad-hoc JSON.

## Key Files

- `scripts/fixtures/intensity-arc/plateaus.action.jsonl` (new)
- `scripts/fixtures/intensity-arc/plateaus.capture.json` (new)
- `scripts/fixtures/intensity-arc/short-band.action.jsonl` (new)
- `scripts/intensity-arc-fixtures.mjs` (new — pure builders)
- `scripts/intensity-arc-fixtures.d.mts` (new — types)
- `scripts/intensity-arc.test.ts` (new — fixture-loading assertions only)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Synthetic fixtures are committed for all four bands, the shortfall case, a header-only series, a sample-less series, a missing anchor, an `approximate` anchor and a two-capture corpus; every series fixture is produced with `serialiseActionIntensitySeries`/`actionIntensitySeriesLine` from `scripts/capture-series.mjs`.
- Fixture loading is pure — filesystem reads of committed files only — so the fixture tests run with no browser, no network and no capture footage.
- The plateau builder turns `[{ fromT, toT, intensity }]` into a series whose sample `intensity` values all land inside the requested band, asserted by a test.
- The fixture tests fail loudly (non-zero) when a fixture drifts from the series schema (header `schemaVersion`/`sampleRateHz` mismatch, or a sample missing `intensity`).

## Impact

Later intensity-arc items can be built test-first against committed, footage-free fixtures instead of hand-crafted ad-hoc JSON.

# Intensity-arc planner: series ingest and band config

**Issue type:** feature · **Priority:** high
**Parent:** AH-0MWPCLYYG007NUJY · first slice of the pure planner (`scripts/intensity-arc.mjs`).

## Goal

A pure planner that loads every capture's recorded action-intensity series and
join anchor, maps series time onto video time, and exposes the single
overridable band/target config object — failing loudly, never silently short,
when a band cannot be filled.

## Scope

- New `scripts/intensity-arc.mjs` + `scripts/intensity-arc.d.mts`.
- **Reuse** these helpers from `scripts/capture-series.mjs` rather than
  re-deriving anything: `ACTION_INTENSITY_SERIES_EXTENSION`,
  `CAPTURE_ANCHOR_EXTENSION`, `hasActionIntensitySample`,
  `actionIntensitySeriesFileName`, `captureAnchorFileName`,
  `captureSeriesStem`.
- `DEFAULT_INTENSITY_ARC_CONFIG` — **the only** definition of the arc
  (`high` 0.65–0.75 / 10 s, `medium` 0.40–0.55 / 7 s, `medium+`
  0.55–0.65 / 7 s, `very high` ≥ 0.75 / 10 s, **in arc order**), plus
  `minWindowSeconds: 1.0`, `fadeSeconds: 0.3` (vidc's
  `DEFAULT_FADE_DURATION_MS`) and `sampleRateHz: 10`. Documented defaults per
  `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §6.6's knob-object pattern.
- **No `--arc` / spec parser.** The arc is not a user-selectable value: the
  intensity arc is the only behaviour of `capture:promo`, so the config object
  is tuned by editing it (a plain Node script, no rebuild). Validation rejects
  a malformed config at module load with an actionable message, so a retune
  cannot ship a broken arc.
- Ingest: for each candidate clip, read `<stem>.action.jsonl` and
  `<stem>.capture.json`; skip header-only/sample-less series and clips whose
  anchor is missing or `approximate` with **exactly one** warning each; fail
  with an actionable error when no usable capture remains.
- Join: `videoTimeMs(t) = t − offsetMs` clamped at 0, exactly as
  `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.5 documents.
- Shared run-length helper (`longestWindowSeconds(band)`) used by both the
  shortfall diagnosis and (in the next item) window assembly.

## Key Files

- `scripts/intensity-arc.mjs` (new)
- `scripts/intensity-arc.d.mts` (new)
- `scripts/intensity-arc.test.ts` (extend)
- `scripts/capture-series.mjs` (reused, unchanged)

## Acceptance Criteria

- The planner loads `<stem>.action.jsonl` + `<stem>.capture.json` per capture, skips header-only/sample-less series and clips with a missing or `approximate` anchor with exactly one warning each, and fails with an actionable error when no usable capture remains; covered by unit tests over committed synthetic fixtures (no browser, no network).
- The four bands and their 7/7/10/10 s targets live in one documented config object, with **no CLI or flag override**; a band that cannot be filled fails naming band, required seconds and the longest available window; unit tested for both the satisfiable and the shortfall case.
- A malformed config object (unknown band name, non-positive duration, unordered arc) is rejected at load with an actionable message, unit tested — a retune can never ship a broken arc silently.
- Series time is mapped to video time with the anchor's `offsetMs` (`videoTimeMs = t − offsetMs`, clamped at 0), unit tested against a fixture whose plateau boundaries are known.

## Assumptions

- Band membership uses the instantaneous `intensity` field with inclusive
  `min` / exclusive `max`, except the top band which is `I ≥ min` (parent item
  assumption 1–2).

## Impact

A producer's recorded intensity series becomes readable, join-anchored data the promo edit can be planned from.
data.title: Intensity-arc planner: series ingest and band config

# Planner window selection and fade compensation

**Issue type:** feature · **Priority:** high
**Parent:** AH-0MWPCLYYG007NUJY · second slice of the pure planner: turn banded footage into the 34 s arc.

## Goal

`planIntensityArc(captures, config)` selects the actual footage windows — the
fewest non-overlapping windows that fill each band, in arc order, with the
fade overlap compensated so the **rendered** timeline totals 34 s.

## Scope

- Extend `scripts/intensity-arc.mjs` with `planIntensityArc(...)` returning an
  ordered plan: `[{ band, sourceStem, inSeconds, durationSeconds, videoTimeSeconds }]`.
- Selection rules:
  - arc order **high → medium → medium+ → very high**;
  - windows are non-overlapping inside a source clip **and** never reused
    across bands (one window per unit of footage);
  - fewest windows per band reaching the target, minimum window length
    `minWindowSeconds` (1.0 s);
  - windows may come from different captures (pooled across the corpus).
- Edge nudging: window boundaries are nudged to local `smoothed` minima within
  a small bounded distance so a cut does not land mid-spike (parent assumption
  2). The bound and the nudge are documented in the module and unit tested.
- Fade compensation: `rendered = Σ durations − (clips − 1) × fadeSeconds`, so
  the planner adds `(clips − 1) × fadeSeconds` of footage, distributed across
  bands, to deliver 34 s rendered. The chosen formula is documented in the
  module and asserted by a test; the binding constraint is the rendered total,
  not any per-band sketch (parent AC3(d), assumption 3).
- Determinism of the plan itself: candidates are ordered by clip natural order,
  then earliest `t`; ties never depend on filesystem iteration order.

## Key Files

- `scripts/intensity-arc.mjs` (extend)
- `scripts/intensity-arc.d.mts` (extend)
- `scripts/intensity-arc.test.ts` (extend)

## Acceptance Criteria

- The chosen windows (a) are non-overlapping within each source clip, (b) are ordered high → medium → medium+ → very high, (c) use the fewest windows reaching each target with a 1.0 s minimum, and (d) produce a rendered-timeline total of 34 s (fade overlap compensated); asserted on synthetic series with known-intensity plateaus plus a property test that no window is reused.
- A band that cannot be filled reports the shortfall (`band, required seconds, longest available window`) from the real selection pass, not from an estimate, and is unit tested on the `short-band` fixture.
- Window boundaries never cut mid-spike: each edge lies within the documented nudge bound of a local `smoothed` minimum, unit tested on a fixture with a spike adjacent to each band edge.
- Re-planning the same captures twice in one process and in a fresh process yields an identical plan array (deep equality); unit tested.

## Assumptions

- The per-band share of the inter-band fade overlap is an implementation
  detail; the AC binds the **rendered total** (34 s) and each band's rendered
  outcome, so the planner may choose the distribution that keeps windows
  contiguous.
- `--fade-duration` is the only softening mechanism (document transitions are
  not rendered yet: VC-0MWNW4SPX002J2SE / VC-0MWNW4T81005YFBJ), so joins are
  hard cuts in the document.

## Impact

A producer gets an arc cut from the measured action — 10 s of high, 7 s medium, 7 s medium+, 10 s very high — instead of filename order.
data.title: Planner window selection and fade compensation

# OTIO document writer for the arc plan

**Issue type:** feature · **Priority:** high
**Parent:** AH-0MWPCLYYG007NUJY · emit the plan as an OpenTimelineIO 0.16.0 document `vidc` can compile.

## Goal

Serialise the arc plan as a valid OTIO 0.16.0 document (`Timeline.1` /
`Track.1` / `Clip.1`) whose clips carry a document-relative `target_url` and a
`source_range` in point, deterministically, so the edit decision is
hand-editable and reproducible.

## Scope

- New `scripts/otio-write.mjs` + `scripts/otio-write.d.mts`:
  `buildOtioDocument(plan, options)` → document object,
  `serialiseOtioDocument(document)` → byte-stable string (2-space JSON, one
  trailing newline).
- Labels `Timeline.1`/`Stack.1`/`Track.1`/`Clip.1`/`TimeRange.1`/
  `RationalTime.1`/`ExternalReference.1` **mirrored** from the `video_compiler`
  model (`src/otio/model.ts`, `OTIO_SCHEMA_VERSION = '0.16.0'`), with a module
  comment naming that repo as the source of truth. Plain JSON, **no new
  dependency** (parent constraint).
- One video track; one `Clip.1` per planned window in arc order.
  `media_reference` is an `ExternalReference.1` whose `target_url` is the clip
  basename relative to the document's directory (`gameplay-….webm`), never an
  absolute path.
- `source_range.start_time` = the window's in point, `source_range.duration` =
  the window length, both `RationalTime.1` at `rate: 30` (vidc's
  `DEFAULT_OTIO_RATE`) with values rounded to whole frames by a documented rule;
  a test pins the quantisation to ±1 frame of the planned window so the ±100 ms
  per-band acceptance tolerance stays reachable.
- `metadata` records the planner inputs: band thresholds, `fadeSeconds`, the
  arc spec, the source stems and the per-band achieved seconds, so an edit is
  auditable.

## Key Files

- `scripts/otio-write.mjs` (new)
- `scripts/otio-write.d.mts` (new)
- `scripts/otio-write.test.ts` (new)
- `scripts/intensity-arc.mjs` (consumes the plan type)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running the planner twice on the same inputs produces a byte-identical `.otio`; ties resolve by clip natural order then earliest `t`; unit tested by double-run comparison.
- The emitted `.otio` parses as `Timeline.1`/`Track.1`/`Clip.1` with one video track, one `Clip.1` per window carrying a document-relative `target_url` and a `source_range` whose start/duration equal the planned window, and is accepted by `vidc timeline`/`vidc render` with no schema diagnostics; the parse assertions are unit tested, the `vidc` acceptance is a documented manual verification step.
- Every emitted `target_url` is a bare basename (no directory, no absolute path) that exists in the capture directory the plan was drawn from; unit tested, including a plan whose windows span two captures.
- `metadata` echoes the band thresholds, fade, arc spec and per-band achieved seconds used for the plan, asserted against the planner's own config object so the document can never record values the plan did not use.

## Assumptions

- Frame quantisation at rate 30 is acceptable: ±16.7 ms per boundary, well
  inside the ±100 ms per-band acceptance tolerance (AC7).

## Impact

A producer can open, tweak and re-render the promo edit in any OTIO editor instead of hand-picking timestamps.
